deployment_requirement.statement: A list length, a business metric for the ordering and a tolerance, declared by the owner of the surface that shows it.

external_referent: A public learning-to-rank dataset (candidates: MSLR-WEB, Yahoo LTR; none chosen) and an independent replication.

robustness.question: Does the ordering hold up under label noise and changed lists?
robustness.perturbation_or_signal: Relevance label noise at 5% and 20%; query lists shortened to half; duplicate documents added.
robustness.truth: Clean-label relevance and a feature-only baseline ranker.
robustness.metric: NDCG at k against the baseline with an interval over queries.
robustness.acceptance_rule: NDCG at k >= baseline plus lift_floor under every perturbation.

drift.question: Is a shift in the relevance distribution noticed?
drift.perturbation_or_signal: A planted change in feature distributions and in the share of relevant items.
drift.metric: Detection rate and false alarms per 1000 null batches on score and feature distributions.
drift.acceptance_rule: Detection rate >= detect_floor and false alarms <= alarm_ceiling.

explanation.question: Do attributions recover what drives relevance?
explanation.perturbation_or_signal: Relevance generated from a known weighted sum of features.
explanation.metric: Rank correlation between attributions and planted weights.

monitoring.question: Can ranking quality be watched when judgments arrive late?
monitoring.perturbation_or_signal: Streams with a planted degradation and a stated judgment delay.
monitoring.truth: The batch at which it began.
monitoring.metric: Detection delay for NDCG at k on judged queries.

parameter_rule: Every null parameter is fixed by the deployment owner and written into this file before the first line of the slice is built; it is never fitted to a result.
not_claimed: any benchmark in this file has been run
